subject: Archaeology
title: Space Archaeology: Beyond Earth
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Space Archaeology: Beyond Earth.

hook.text: The Moon has archaeological sites. Landing spots and footprints are heritage — unprotected.

buildup.text: Apollo 11's boot prints, flag, and equipment have not been touched since 1969.

discovery.text: NASA's 2020 act asks lunar visitors to avoid Apollo sites but cannot enforce it.

twist.text: Private companies plan Moon missions. Nothing stops a rover driving over the prints.

climax.text: Archaeologists want lunar heritage protected like Earth sites. Space is next.

punchline.text: We left footprints on the Moon. No law protects them.

quiz.question: What is the legal status of Apollo landing sites?
options: Fully protected under space heritage treaties
NASA asks visitors to avoid them but no binding law exists
They belong to the United States under the Outer Space Treaty
